Changelog

This document records all notable changes to RAPAS Photometry Pipeline.

Version 1.9.0

Released: October 15, 2026

(Version 1.8.8 was not released; Version 1.8.9 followed 1.8.7 directly.)

Login audit log

  • Every successful login writes a timestamped line with the pipeline version to the service log: [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] RPP vX.Y.Z - User '<username>' logged in successfully (<origin>).

  • api/main.py (FastAPI backend), backend.py (legacy backend) and pages/login.py (frontend) each emit their own line; the origin suffix tells them apart. The version is read at runtime from src/__version__.py, so the message follows future releases automatically.

Curated catalog export

  • Fixed export columns. *_catalog.csv and *_catalog.vot now contain only id, ra, dec, the Astro-Colibri, SIMBAD, SkyBoT and AAVSO matches, catalog_matches, x_center, y_center, snr_*, the aperture magnitudes with their quality_flag_*, the PSF magnitude, the magnitude errors and the psf_minus_aperture_mag_* offsets, in that order. Radius suffixes (third aperture = user choice) and the filter prefix (for example rapasg_) are resolved dynamically; absent columns are skipped. Colour-corrected columns and internal diagnostics are no longer written to the files (they remain available in the session).

  • Astro-Colibri first. Rows with an astrocolibri_name are sorted at the top of both files.

  • Unique source ``id``. id is the first column, complete (PSF-only sources get new numbers) and unique; x_center/y_center are filled from the detection centroid for PSF-only sources.

  • Aladin ID. The ID shown in the Aladin Lite popup is always the id column of the files (created when missing).

  • Transient CSV. *_transients.csv reuses the catalog columns, matching each candidate to its catalog source by sky position (the previous match by rounded pixel coordinates could silently miss sources).

  • New helpers ensure_source_ids, build_export_columns and prepare_export_table in src/utils.py, build_transient_table in src/transient.py, and tests/test_export_catalog.py.

Transient finder filter association, sparse-field detection

  • Calibration band -> catalogue column fix. The transient finder guessed the filter from the calibration column name with a substring search, so Gaia RP was read as r (PS1 rmag), Gaia BP and the Johnson V/B bands matched nothing (every match was then silently confirmed) and Gaia G was compared with the PS1-transformed gmag. A new normalize_calibration_filter maps each calibration band explicitly (phot_g/bp/rp_mean_mag -> G/BP/RP, *_jkc_mag -> U/V/B/R/I, u_sdss_mag -> u, gmag… -> g…) so the native Gaia columns are used.

  • Gaia r vs g consistency. For raw Vizier Gaia tables r/R/V now map to Gmag (as in the XMatch branch) instead of BPmag.

  • Astrometry: 2 sigma when 3 sigma is sparse. A 3 sigma detection with fewer than 100 sources is no longer accepted directly: 2 sigma is tried and kept when it finds more sources (otherwise the 3 sigma list is used).

  • Transient candidates in Aladin. Candidates are drawn as yellow stars in a dedicated “Transient candidates” overlay of the Aladin Lite widget (popup with the catalogue id, coordinates and PSF magnitude) for visual checking, next to the red Astro-Colibri squares.

  • Transient finder at 1.5 sigma. Detection now starts directly at 1.5 sigma (TRANSIENT_DETECT_THRESH) with a minimum S/N of 2 (3 above 2 sigma) to be more sensitive to faint sources. Candidates are still required to match the photometry table.

  • Transient finder without PSF photometry. When the photometry table has no PSF magnitude columns, or when the matched detections have no finite PSF value, find_candidates() now falls back to the calibrated 1.1 x FWHM aperture magnitude (aperture_mag_1_1 and its error) instead of aborting with “No transient candidates found”. The app displays a warning when candidates rely on this fallback, using the same PSF-unavailable wording as the main pipeline. The shared warning is PSF photometry is not available; using calibrated aperture photometry instead.; the full transient variant is PSF photometry is not available; using calibrated aperture photometry instead. Transient candidates use the calibrated 1.1 x FWHM aperture magnitude.

Finer astrometry and Astro-Colibri radius

  • Detection ladder 3 -> 2 -> 1 sigma. The blind solve now targets at least 20 stars (Astrometry.net has no hard minimum: it builds quads from the brightest sources first, so about 20 well-measured stars is the practical target). The detection threshold is lowered from 3 to 2 and then 1 sigma until the target is reached, with the measurement S/N relaxed accordingly (5, 3, 2). The small-image floor is raised from 10 to 20.

  • Best effort on sparse fields. If no threshold reaches the target, the richest detection with at least 5 stars is used instead of failing, with a warning in the log.

  • Retry on failure. When the local solve fails, detection is repeated at the next lower threshold and the solve is retried before the online fallback.

  • Astro-Colibri progressive radius. Events are matched at 5 arcsec, then 10, 15 and 20 arcsec (was a fixed 10 arcsec); the log lists how many events were matched at each radius, and a WARNING is raised for matches only found at the 15 or 20 arcsec tier. New astrocolibri_match_radius helper and tests in tests/test_robustness_astrometry.py and tests/test_network_resilience.py.

  • Astro-Colibri sources listed and highlighted. The event RA/Dec are kept (astrocolibri_ra / astrocolibri_dec columns, exported after astrocolibri_classification), every event returned for the field is displayed in a table (including events without coordinates), and cross-matched sources are drawn as larger red squares in a dedicated Aladin Lite layer.

  • Richer Astro-Colibri events and errors. The events table now also shows observatory, trigger ID, position error (arcsec), date and redshift when the API provides them; sources / xsources / icecat entries are reported in the log; HTTP 401/403/429 answers give an explicit reason and the response is parsed defensively.

  • More robust SkyBoT queries. New shared skybot_cone_search helper (src/utils.py) used by the catalog cross-match and the transient filter: 3 attempts on network errors and HTTP 429/5xx, -from label, epoch range check, HTTP error reporting, mid-exposure epoch and a per-object match tolerance of 10 to 30 arcsec derived from the ephemeris Err.

PSF, Transients and Messages

  • PSF star minimum lowered from 15 to 10. A warning about possibly poor PSF quality is shown when fewer than 25 PSF stars are available.

  • Transient finder accepts ``uint16`` images. The image is converted to float32 before SEP background estimation and extraction (SEP rejects uint16).

  • SCAMP refinement retries on too few matches. SCAMP’s default POSITION_MAXERR (1 arcmin) made refinement report “0 reference matches” when the plate solution was slightly off. A second attempt now widens POSITION_MAXERR/PIXSCALE_MAXERR/POSANGLE_MAXERR and relaxes SN_THRESHOLDS.

  • Cleaner messages. The ASTRiDE candidate/diagnostic messages were removed, and the zero-point summary now reads Zero Point: X ± σ, calibrator scatter = S mag.

Astro-Colibri cross-match and cutouts

  • Nearest-event matching. Astro-Colibri events are matched to the closest catalog source within 10 arcsec (match_to_catalog_sky); events without coordinates are ignored.

  • Visible outcome. The number of matches (or none, or service unavailable) is displayed in the app instead of only in the log.

  • Cutouts with magnitude. plot_astrocolibri_cutouts uses the WCS for pixel positions, circles the source, and shows its calibrated magnitude (filter-prefixed columns are now recognised).

  • Hemisphere-aware template. The HiPS template is fetched from PanSTARRS (north) or SkyMapper (south) and falls back to the other survey when the field is not covered.

Session Isolation (concurrent users)

  • Per-session work folders. Every browser session now gets its own work_<id> folder, both for temporary uploads (/tmp/<user>/work_<id>/) and for intermediate results (rpp_results/<user>_results/work_<id>/). Two sessions, including two sessions of the same account, can no longer overwrite or pick up each other’s FITS files, headers or intermediate products. Final ZIP archives stay in the user-level rpp_results/<user>_results/ folder.

  • Reset works in one press. The uploader widget is re-keyed on every reset, so the previously loaded file is dropped immediately instead of requiring a second click. Reset is now session-local: it only clears the current session’s state and folders and no longer calls the global st.cache_data.clear() that affected every connected user.

  • Run trigger consumed at start. The Start Analysis trigger is cleared as soon as a run begins, so a failed or interrupted run cannot silently restart on the next interaction.

  • Safer download matching. Prefix matching of result files only pools files whose name continues with a delimiter (_, ., -), so image1 no longer collects the files of image10.

Stale-File Cleanup

  • Work folders and loose temporary uploads older than 24 hours (left by closed browsers or abandoned analyses) are removed once per session after login. Archived ZIP files are never touched, and the current session is always preserved.

Cached FITS Parser and Shared State

  • The cached FITS parser is now pure: it returns the data, header and a list of messages, and load_fits_data replays those messages in the calling session, so cached results no longer leak UI messages or state across users.

  • Matplotlib figures are closed after being displayed and after being saved, avoiding the process-wide figure registry being shared between sessions; the temporary ASTRiDE directory is removed after use.

  • Shared astroquery clients (Gaia main table, Skybot raw-response flag) are configured once at import instead of inside each function.

Tests and Documentation

  • New tests/test_session_isolation.py plus UI regression tests covering session folders, cleanup, delimiter matching, the pure parser and the import-time astroquery configuration.

  • README, features, troubleshooting and tutorial pages (English and French) describe session isolation, Reset and stale-file cleanup.

Version 1.8.7

Released: October 7, 2026

Effective-Gain Resolution

  • ``CVF`` conversion factor supported. The FITS CVF keyword is now read and converted with gain = 1/CVF. Explicit conversion keywords (EGAIN/CCDGAIN in e-/ADU and CVF) are tried before the conventional GAIN, so a driver setting written to GAIN can no longer shadow a genuine conversion keyword.

  • Driver-gain cameras recognised. On QHY (abstract 0-100 scale; a QHY268M reaches ≈0.77 e-/ADU at GAIN=56) and ZWO ASI (0.1 dB scale) cameras the bare GAIN value is a driver setting rather than e-/ADU and is now ignored: the pipeline falls back to EGAIN/CVF, the user-supplied gain, or the frame’s own photon-transfer estimate. The recognised cameras are listed in the editable DRIVER_GAIN_INSTRUMENT_PATTERNS.

  • Plausible gain range widened 0.02-20 → 0.02-100 e-/ADU, so cameras with a genuinely large conversion factor are no longer rejected; the driver-setting guard, not the range, is what rejects QHY/ZWO values. The Detector Gain control accepts up to 1000 e-/ADU.

  • One resolver everywhere. src/astrometry.py and src/transient.py now call resolve_effective_gain() instead of the old 65535 / max(image) heuristic, so EGAIN/CVF/driver handling is consistent across photometry, cosmic-ray masking and SEP detection.

  • Tests: CVF inversion, keyword precedence, driver-camera detection (including a false-positive guard) and the widened range are covered by new cases in tests/test_photometry.py.

  • Documentation: the photometry-formulas, features and tutorial pages (English and French) and the README describe the new gain resolution.

Pixel Scale and Login

  • No silent 1 arcsec/pixel default. When the pixel scale cannot be read from the header or computed from the solved WCS, the run stops and asks for the new Pixel scale override value (sidebar, Parameters).

  • The CD-matrix pixel scale uses column norms (valid for rotated matrices) and ignores non-numeric keywords.

  • The login page reminds Firefox users to press Enter after typing the password.

Version 1.8.6

Released: October 4, 2026

Transient Candidate Selection

  • SEP detection flags are now actually applied. The candidate filter was called with stdpipe’s default flag mask (0x7F00), which only matches stdpipe/SExtractor flag bits; raw SEP flags live in the low byte, so the mask never matched and no detection was ever flag-filtered. find_candidates() now passes SEP_REJECT_FLAGS (0xDE: object or aperture truncated at the frame boundary, deblending overflow, degenerate centroid, all-masked or non-positive aperture), so unreliable detections are discarded.

  • Seeing-based cross-match radius. SEP detections are matched to the pipeline photometry catalog within a seeing-sized radius (clip(FWHM, 1, 4) arcsec) instead of a fixed 10 arcsec. Because spherical_match() returns all pairs inside the radius, the old value produced many-to-many matches in crowded fields, duplicating candidates and attaching the wrong PSF magnitude; only the nearest counterpart is now kept.

  • Correct catalogue matching radius in ``filter_transient_candidates()``. The function was previously given an already arcsec-scaled FWHM and no pixscale, so the radius silently fell back to a fixed 1 arcsec. It now receives the FWHM in pixels and pixscale in degrees/pixel, giving the intended half-FWHM radius.

  • Brightness-excess test documented and configurable. checker_fn() follows stdpipe’s contract (a True entry is a confirmed catalogue match that removes the detection); the docstring now states this explicitly and the excess threshold was exposed as mag_threshold (default 2.0 mag). Detections whose magnitude difference cannot be evaluated are kept instead of being silently discarded.

  • Tests: the SEP flag mask and the candidate-checker semantics are covered by new cases in tests/test_new_features.py.

Documentation

  • The user guide, advanced-features and API reference pages, the English and French tutorials, and the README now describe the current transient candidate algorithm (SEP flag filtering, seeing-based cross-matching and the brightness-excess rule).

Version 1.8.5

Released: October 2, 2026

Transient Candidate Filtering

  • Removed the minimum S/N filter from transient-candidate selection so that low-S/N detections remain eligible. The other catalog, known-source, Solar System-object, and magnitude-error validity filters remain in place.

PSF Photometry Reliability

  • Star selection no longer silently skips PSF photometry. The “adaptive” S/N threshold was computed from sqrt(flux) when no per-source S/N or flux_err was available, and then kept only the top half of the candidates. That is not a quality measure, and combined with the median..90th-percentile flux window it left fewer than the minimum 15 stars on clean fields, so the entire PSF step was dropped. The approximate-S/N cut is now skipped (the flux window already keeps the bright half).

  • Saturation filter relaxed. The previous limit min(peak_85 * 0.95, img_max * 0.85) rejected the brightest unsaturated stars, which are exactly the best ePSF stars. Truly saturated pixels are already flagged by the pipeline mask before detection, so this is now only a last-resort guard that trims peaks within 0.5% of the frame maximum.

  • On a clean 121-star field that previously produced only 14 candidates (below the 15-star minimum, so PSF photometry was skipped), 49 stars are now selected and PSF photometry runs on all 121 detected sources.

PSF Shape and Dimensions

  • Fitting region rounded, not truncated. int(3 * fwhm) shifted the effective aperture radius by up to half a pixel; it now uses round.

  • ePSF extracted from a larger cutout. The empirical PSF was built from a 3 x FWHM cutout whose radius equals the largest aperture used for the encircled-energy correction, so its wings were truncated and normalised away. It is now extracted from a 5 x FWHM cutout, so both the aperture-correction curve and the fitted fluxes reflect the real PSF wings; the fit itself still uses the compact fit_shape.

  • Model-centre convention fixed. The centre of an N-pixel grid is (N - 1) / 2, not N / 2. The old value reported a spurious half/oversampled-pixel peak offset (and could trigger an unnecessary re-centering that shifted the model off-centre).

  • Aperture correction uses the fitted PSF. After an optional re-centering the returned / st.session_state["epsf_model"] model is now the exact object used for the fits, so the encircled-energy correction can no longer be derived from a stale (non-re-centred) PSF.

PSF-vs-Aperture Consistency Diagnostic

  • A new check_psf_aperture_consistency() helper matches PSF and aperture sources by position and reports the median psf_mag - aperture_mag for each aperture. Because both methods share the total-flux scale, a median offset larger than PSF_APERTURE_CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD (0.15 mag) is now reported as a warning; the per-aperture counts, offsets and robust scatter are stored in st.session_state["psf_aperture_consistency"].

  • Per-source offset columns: the same difference is exported for every aperture as psf_minus_aperture_mag_X_X (with filter-prefixed aliases) and is left NaN where only one method measured the source.

  • Plotted diagnostic: the results view renders the per-source psf_mag - aperture_mag offset – a scatter against the calibrated PSF magnitude with the per-aperture median and zero lines, plus the offset histogram – and saves it next to the other diagnostics as <base>_psf_aperture_offset.png.

  • Catalog cross-match robustness: SkyBoT requests VOTable output and skips malformed service-error responses instead of reporting them as empty fields. The 10 Parsec catalog’s proper motions are propagated to the observation epoch when available, and Aladin popups include SkyBoT and nearby-star identifications.

  • Gaia DR3 fallback reliability: the VizieR fallback now queries the Gaia DR3 cone-search catalog and uses its returned results. The direct TAP query no longer orders by an unsupported DISTANCE() expression.

  • Crowded-field local background left unchanged by design: an empirical check showed that zeroing the per-source local background for sources with overlapping fit_shape regions biases crowded fluxes ~5-7% high, while keeping it recovers the true flux, so no guard was applied.

Documentation

  • docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md, docs/features.rst, docs/advanced_features.rst and docs/api_reference.rst document the selection, ePSF-extraction and consistency-diagnostic changes; the English and French tutorials note the new diagnostic.

  • Regression tests cover the field that previously skipped PSF photometry, the ePSF centring, and the consistency diagnostic.

Version 1.8.4

Released: October 2, 2026

Configuration Persistence

  • New sidebar parameters are persisted and restored: the Max Magnitude Error (mag_err_max) and Detector Gain (effective_gain) controls are written into analysis_parameters, so they are saved with the rest of the settings and reloaded at the next login. The two keys are now also seeded in default_analysis_params (src/tools_app.py).

  • Round-trip coverage: the full save/reload path is now tested for both the FastAPI (/api/config) and legacy Flask (/save_config / /get_config) backends in tests/test_config_persistence.py, alongside structural checks of the save/load wiring in pages/app.py and pages/login.py.

  • Legacy backend dependencies declared: flask and flask-cors are now listed in pyproject.toml and requirements.txt so the legacy backend and its tests work in a fresh install.

Documentation

  • The English and French tutorials now document the Max Magnitude Error and Detector Gain parameters.

  • docs/api.rst documents the FastAPI versus legacy Flask configuration-persistence paths; docs/advanced_features.rst adds configuration-persistence and testing sections; docs/installation.rst and docs/features.rst cover the backend dependencies and the both-backend persistence.

  • Corrected several RST section underlines that were shorter than their titles.

Version 1.8.3

Released: October 1, 2026

Follow-up to the error-budget review (docs/ERROR_BUDGET_REVIEW.md).

Photometry Error Budget

  • Local-background uncertainty uses the median estimator: the annulus uncertainty is now ApertureStats.median_err (√(π/2)·s/√A_ann) instead of the mean-based std/√A_ann. Using the mean’s standard error for a median under-estimated the local term by ~25% (about 8% of σ_flux in the background-limited regime). The mean-based value is kept only as a fallback when median_err is unavailable.

  • Aperture-correction systematic: every aperture magnitude error now includes σ_apcorr = 1.0857 · f_apcorr · |apcorr − 1| / apcorr (APCORR_SYSTEMATIC_FRACTION, default 0.20), exported as apcorr_mag_err_X_X. The correction previously shifted the magnitude with no error attached, so the systematic was invisible at high S/N.

  • Global systematic floor wired through: SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR is now passed to add_calibrated_magnitudes via resolve_systematic_floor() (session state / RPP_SYSTEMATIC_MAG_ERR_FLOOR / module default).

  • Color-term uncertainty propagated: fit_color_term_correction returns the fit parameter covariance (plus intercept_std / color_term_std), and apply_color_term_correction writes color_term_offset_err and a *_colorcorr_err column (√(σ_mag_calib² + σ_color_term_offset²)) for every corrected magnitude, with filter-prefixed aliases.

  • Random vs correlated components: calibrated magnitude errors now carry *_mag_err_*_random (per-source) and *_mag_err_*_correlated (field-common zero-point/systematic) columns in addition to the total error.

  • Centroid-position term: the aperture flux error now includes a centroid contribution. σ_pos = σ_PSF / S/N (floored, capped at 0.5×FWHM) and the flux change for a one-sigma displacement is measured by re-evaluating the aperture shifted by ±σ_pos along x and y, capturing the real PSF asymmetry (centroid_flux_err_X_X).

  • Zero-point uncertainty de-biased: the scatter used for σ_zp is now taken from the sigma-clipped sample before the |residual| <= 0.5 mag hard cut, which truncated the distribution and biased the uncertainty low. Both scatter estimates and N are stored in st.session_state["zero_point_diagnostics"].

Noise Model and Background

  • The last-resort constant background model (_constant_background) now uses the same MAD-based RMS as the normal Background2D path, so crowded frames that trigger the fallback do not get a source-inflated noise map.

  • The source-detection threshold is now derived from the MAD-based global scatter (stdfunc="mad_std") instead of the plain sigma-clipped standard deviation, so detection and the error model use the same robust noise estimate and the effective threshold is not raised by undetected sources.

PSF Photometry

  • A per-source local background (LocalBackground, sigma-clipped median annulus, 2×–3× FWHM) is now subtracted before the PSF fits; sources whose annulus is fully masked or off-frame fall back to no subtraction rather than a NaN fit.

  • The empirical PSF is built from de-contaminated star cutouts: the same local background is removed from a copy of the image around each PSF star before extract_stars, so the ePSF is not constructed from sky-contaminated stars. On a synthetic sky-pedestal frame the recovered PSF flux bias drops from ×2.5 (no local background) to ×1.001.

Observability

  • ee_fraction_X_X is exported next to apcorr_X_X so the aperture correction is auditable.

  • The misleading zero_point_error column was renamed to zero_point_scatter; zero_point_std is now exported as a catalog column, while zero_point_scatter, zero_point_scatter_kept and zero_point_n are recorded on the matched calibration table.

  • Consistent prefixed error-component export: drop_legacy_magnitude_columns now also removes the legacy psf_mag_err_random / psf_mag_err_correlated columns when a filter prefix applies, so the PSF error components are replaced by their prefixed aliases just like the aperture ones (aperture_mag_err_*_random / _correlated) instead of surviving unprefixed alongside them.

  • Colour-corrected columns kept consistently: aperture_mag_X_X_colorcorr_err is no longer mistaken for a legacy aperture magnitude and dropped under a filter prefix; both the legacy and prefixed *_colorcorr / *_colorcorr_err columns are exported in parallel.

Version 1.8.1

Released: September 29, 2026

Photometry Error Budget

  • Consistent flux for S/N, magnitude and error: the S/N, instrumental magnitude and magnitude error are now all derived from one flux — the background-subtracted, aperture-corrected aperture sum. Previously the magnitude used the background-corrected flux while its error used the raw aperture sum, which diverged whenever the local background was not ~0.

  • Local-background error propagation: the uncertainty of the sigma-clipped annulus background is added to the flux error in quadrature (σ_flux² = σ_aperture² + σ_total_bkg²). This removes a systematic under-estimate of the error and over-estimate of the S/N of roughly 20% for the default annulus geometry.

  • Robust local background: the annulus background is now a sigma-clipped median (ApertureStats) rather than a plain mean, so neighbours and cosmic rays no longer bias it.

  • Masked-pixel handling: the pipeline mask (border, cosmic rays, satellite trails and NaNs) is now applied to both the source and the annulus photometry, and the exact masked-pixel area (area_overlap) is used.

  • Aperture correction: an encircled-energy correction derived from the empirical PSF (analytic Gaussian fallback) puts aperture and PSF photometry on the same total-flux scale. The factor is stored in the apcorr_X_X column.

  • Zero-point error propagation: calibrated magnitude errors now combine the instrumental and zero-point uncertainties in quadrature (σ_mag_calib = √(σ_mag_inst² + σ_zp²)), and the zero point is no longer rounded to two decimals.

  • Correct zero-point uncertainty for a median estimator: the zero point is a median, so its formal uncertainty now carries the √(π/2) median factor (zero_point_std = 1.2533 × scatter / √N) instead of the mean-based scatter / √N, which under-estimated it by ~20%. Exported as MEDIAN_STD_ERROR_FACTOR in src.pipeline.

  • Unreliable-photometry cut is now a last resort: a source is removed only when every photometry method reports a magnitude error of 2 mag or more (MAG_ERR_MAX, up from 1 mag); a source with one usable method is kept, and sources carrying no error information at all (all NaN) are kept as well. The previous all-columns requirement deleted sources that still had a valid aperture (or PSF) measurement. The threshold is exposed as the Max Magnitude Error parameter, and 0 disables the cut entirely.

Noise Model

  • The effective gain for calc_total_error is read from the FITS GAIN/EGAIN keyword; when it is missing or invalid the data are treated as electrons (effective_gain = 1) instead of the previous arbitrary 65535 / max(image) heuristic.

  • Gain resolution order and empirical estimation: when the header carries no usable gain, the pipeline now falls back to a user-supplied value (the Detector Gain sidebar parameter, analysis_parameters["effective_gain"] or the RPP_EFFECTIVE_GAIN environment variable) and then to an empirical photon-transfer estimate computed from the frame itself (1/slope of a robust variance-vs-signal fit on source-free sky boxes, accepted only when the sky level constrains it at ≥ 3σ and the result is physically plausible). Assuming gain = 1 for ADU data overestimates the source Poisson variance by the true gain, i.e. the magnitude errors of bright sources by up to √gain; that silent overestimate is now avoided whenever the gain can be measured or supplied.

Sky Background Model

  • Robust noise map: the per-box background RMS now uses the MAD-based estimator (MADStdBackgroundRMS) instead of the plain sigma-clipped standard deviation. Undetected sources in the boxes used to inflate the noise map by x1.11 / x1.38 / x2.03 at 15 / 12 / 10 px source spacing on synthetic frames, and that factor propagated directly into every flux error.

  • Adaptive smoothing: the median filter applied to the background mesh is capped at 3x3 when the mesh is small (< 12 boxes across). A 5x5 filter over an 8x8 mesh over-smoothed the model: on a 300 ADU sky ramp the subtracted frame was x2.24 noisier than the raw frame, vs x1.54 with a 3x3 filter.

  • No more aborted runs on hard frames: Background2D rejects any box with more than 10 % masked/clipped pixels (exclude_percentile) and raised a ValueError when that excluded every box, which happens for crowded fields and frames with large bad areas. The estimation is now retried with 50 % and 100 % tolerance and with a coarser box, and falls back to a single sigma-clipped background level when no mesh can be built, so photometry still runs. The chosen fallback is reported to the user.

  • Background plot failure is no longer fatal: a missing background figure no longer calls st.pyplot(None).

Bug Fixes

  • The local-background-flatness filter used for PSF model star selection compared the local background scatter to the (near-zero) local median of the sky-subtracted image, which could reject every candidate star and silently skip PSF photometry. It now compares the local scatter to the global background scatter.

  • Cosmic-ray detection used a non-physical gain: mask_and_remove_cosmic_rays passed the raw GAIN value to astroscrappy.detect_cosmics. On a real 900 s frame carrying GAIN=56 (a QHY driver setting, not e-/ADU) the predicted sky noise was ~1.8 ADU against a real 13.3 ADU, so 49% of the frame was flagged as cosmic rays and excluded from detection and photometry. The routine now uses the resolved effective gain (plus a RDNOISE/READNOIS/ENOISE value when available) and discards an unphysical mask covering more than MAX_CR_MASK_FRACTION (20%) of the frame instead of deleting a large part of the science image. On that frame the mask went from 49.0% to 0.011% of the pixels, detections from 236 to 312, and the calibrator scatter from 0.235 to 0.050 mag.

  • ``GAIN`` no longer hides a valid ``EGAIN``: the keyword scan stopped at the first present key, so a frame with GAIN=0 and EGAIN=3.12 (Moravian cameras) fell through to effective_gain = 1. Invalid values are now skipped in favour of the next candidate keyword.

  • Implausible gains are rejected: values outside 0.02-20 e-/ADU (GAIN_PLAUSIBLE_RANGE) are reported and ignored, because a detector driver setting used as a gain inflates the S/N of bright sources by up to ~7x and corrupts the cosmic-ray mask.

  • validate_cross_match_results() read a gaia_separation_arcsec column that the cross-match never writes (it writes catalog_separation_arcsec), so the median-separation sanity check was a no-op, and the function was never called at all. It now reads the real column (legacy alias accepted), tolerates missing coordinates, and is wired into the calibration workflow, which warns the user when the matches are clustered or show an unusually large median separation.

New Output Columns

  • aperture_sum_bkg_corr_err_X_X: error of the background-subtracted flux, including the local-background term.

  • apcorr_X_X: aperture-correction factor applied to each aperture.

Version 1.8.0

Released: September 29, 2026

Photometric Calibration

  • Gaia VizieR fallback: When the Gaia TAP service is unavailable or returns an error, the pipeline now automatically retries the query against the VizieR mirror with a reduced column set, keeping photometric calibration available during TAP outages.

  • Zero-point calibration improvements:

    • Sigma clipping is applied before the final zero-point fit.

    • Sources with residuals beyond ±0.5 mag from the median are excluded before the fit.

    • Aperture 1.3× FWHM is used as the primary reference aperture for zero-point determination.

  • Color-term calibration:

    • The pipeline can now fit a simple first-order color term from matched calibration stars when the selected calibration band has a supported catalog color.

    • Supported color definitions currently include Gaia BP-RP and the Sloan-style colors g-r, r-i, and i-z.

    • Color-corrected magnitudes are written as parallel *_colorcorr columns instead of replacing the baseline zero-point-calibrated magnitudes.

New Functions

  • ``plot_astrocolibri_cutouts()``: Generates postage-stamp cutout images for Astro-Colibri transient candidates directly from the science frame, enabling rapid visual inspection alongside catalog alerts.

  • ``drop_legacy_magnitude_columns()``: Utility to strip the legacy (non-prefixed) magnitude columns from the output catalog when only filter-prefixed aliases are needed.

Robustness & Testing

  • Backend detection improvements: Enhanced probing and fallback logic for FastAPI / legacy backend auto-detection; new tests/test_backend_detection.py covers probe and fallback scenarios.

  • Graceful stdpipe import handling: ImportError from optional stdpipe components is caught and reported cleanly rather than crashing the module load.

Infrastructure

  • Gunicorn UvicornWorker by default: gunicorn.conf.py now sets uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker, preventing WSGI/ASGI mismatches.

  • Dependency cleanup: Removed unused mpmath dependency; tightened setuptools version constraints for reproducible builds.

UI & Logging

  • Consistent Streamlit message levels: Messages use success / warning / info / error severity throughout the pipeline.

  • Reduced log noise: Verbose debug messages removed from the hot path.

  • FITS excluded from download list: .fits files are no longer shown among the per-analysis download buttons.

  • Archived ZIP lazy loading: The sidebar archive browser now lists historical ZIP files without reading them at page load; a ZIP is read only when the user explicitly requests that specific archived download.

  • FWHM sampling: Source sample size increased to 1 250 for better seeing measurement stability.

External Catalog Robustness

  • SkyBoT malformed-response fallback: If SkyBoT returns an unreadable payload, the pipeline now logs a warning and continues without SkyBoT matches instead of surfacing an unexpected processing error.

Documentation

  • New FastAPI + Gunicorn troubleshooting section added to docs/troubleshooting.rst.

Version 1.7.0

Released: 2026

Application Workflow & Stability

  • Explicit Start Gate: Uploading a FITS file now stages it in the Streamlit UI without immediately triggering FITS loading, WCS checks, or photometry. Scientific processing starts only after clicking Start Analysis.

  • Astrometry Toggle Fix: The frontend now reads the astrometry option from the persisted analysis settings, so the sidebar toggle consistently controls forced astrometry checks.

  • Safer Astrometry Fallback: The upload/start workflow no longer passes an unset temporary file path into the astrometry step during the pre-start phase.

Catalog & Network Handling

  • SkyBoT Timeout Adjustment: SkyBoT queries in both catalog enhancement and transient filtering now use a 120-second timeout instead of the previous 300-second default.

  • Graceful Remote-Service Behavior: User-facing documentation and workflow descriptions were aligned with the existing behavior of continuing with partial results when optional remote services are slow, empty, or unavailable.

Packaging & Environment

  • Local Editable Install: Updated requirements.txt to install the local checkout with -e . instead of pointing back to a remote repository URL.

  • Frontend Entry Point: Added run_frontend.py so the configured pfr script entry point resolves correctly.

  • Tooling Target Update: Updated Black configuration to target Python 3.12.

Documentation Refresh

  • Updated README.md and docs/TUTORIAL.md to reflect the staged upload workflow, backend auto-detection, account features, maintenance scripts, astrometry fallback behavior, and partial-result handling.

  • Updated the main Sphinx pages including installation.rst, usage.rst, troubleshooting.rst, features.rst, examples.rst, api_reference.rst, user_guide.rst, advanced_features.rst, api.rst, and index.rst.

  • Replaced outdated terminology such as old start-button labels and stale API/module references with the current code paths and workflow names.

Version 1.5.3

Released: January 7, 2026

Photometry Calculation Improvements

  • Critical Bug Fix: Fixed PSF S/N calculation that was incorrectly using sqrt(flux_err) instead of flux_err. This was causing incorrect S/N values and magnitude errors for all PSF photometry.

  • Precision Enhancement: Removed S/N rounding to preserve full floating-point precision and avoid divide-by-zero errors in magnitude error calculations.

  • Improved S/N Accuracy: S/N now uses background-corrected flux (aperture_sum_bkg_corr) when available, providing more accurate estimates especially for faint sources.

  • Error Propagation: Added proper zero-point error propagation in calibrated magnitudes using quadrature: σ_mag_calib = √(σ_mag_inst² + σ_zp²)

  • Quality Flags: Added photometric quality flags for both aperture and PSF photometry:

    • 'good': S/N > 10 (reliable photometry)

    • 'marginal': 5 < S/N ≤ 10 (use with caution)

    • 'poor': S/N ≤ 5 (unreliable)

    • 'unknown': missing data

Documentation & Testing

  • Comprehensive mathematical documentation of S/N and magnitude error formulas

  • New documentation file: docs/PHOTOMETRY_FORMULAS.md

  • Complete unit test suite: tests/test_photometry.py

  • Inline formula documentation in source code

Technical Details

  • S/N Formula: S/N = flux / flux_error

  • Magnitude Error Formula: σ_mag = 1.0857 × (σ_flux / flux) where 1.0857 = 2.5/ln(10)

  • Calibrated Error: σ_mag_calib = √(σ_mag_inst² + σ_zp²)
